name: Calf's-Foot Jelly
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: 3 cups of sugar—or sweeten to taste
ingredients.originalText: 3 cups of sugar—or sweeten to taste
ingredients.quantityText: 3 cups of sugar—or sweeten to taste

ingredients.name: Juice of 1 lemon, and half the grated peel
ingredients.originalText: Juice of 1 lemon, and half the grated peel

instructions.text: Boil the calf's feet in the water until it is reduced one half
Strain the liquor, and let it stand ten or twelve hours
Skim off every particle of the fat, and remove the dregs
Melt slowly in a porcelain or bell-metal kettle, add the seasoning, sugar, and the whipped whites of the eggs, and boil fast about twelve minutes, skimming well
Strain through a double flannel bag suspended between the four legs of an upturned high stool or backless chair, the bowl set beneath
Do not squeeze or shake it, until the jelly ceases to run freely

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Boil the calf's feet in the water until it is reduced one half
2. Strain the liquor, and let it stand ten or twelve hours
3. Skim off every particle of the fat, and remove the dregs
4. Melt slowly in a porcelain or bell-metal kettle, add the seasoning, sugar, and the whipped whites of the eggs, and boil fast about twelve minutes, skimming well
5. Strain through a double flannel bag suspended between the four legs of an upturned high stool or backless chair, the bowl set beneath
6. Do not squeeze or shake it, until the jelly ceases to run freely
